paper_title: Detecting Dark Matter with Superconducting Nanowires
notes: Paper (Hochberg et al., arXiv:1903.05101) reports a NEW 95% C.L. bound on relic dark photon absorption (kinetic mixing kappa vs m_V) from a 4.3 ng WSi superconducting nanowire prototype with 0.8 eV threshold and 10^4 s exposure with zero dark counts (blue 'Bound WSi' curve in Fig. 4). The paper also reports a new DM-electron scattering bound (sigma_e, Fig. 3) and various future projections (NbN/WSi kg-yr etc.), but the headline result is the dark photon absorption bound, matching the pre-analysis hint. No numerical table is provided; the emitted data points are approximate values reconstructed from the described figure (bound spans ~0.8 eV threshold up to a few eV, kappa at the few x10^-9 level), hence the reduced extraction confidence. DM density explicitly assumed rho_DM = 0.3 GeV/cm^3. Recommend digitizing Fig. 4 for precise values. | selector: text over figure_vision (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0.45, 7))
